title: Sync between devices
summary: A learner's phone and computer keep one set of data in step, directly over the local network.
description: One learner, several devices, no server and no account. Whole rows sync, and every device reaches the same result whatever order changes arrive in.

stories.as: a learner with a phone and a computer
stories.want: both to show the same progress without an account or a server
stories.soThat: I can practise on whichever is at hand

stories.as: a learner who lost a phone
stories.want: to remove it from my devices
stories.soThat: it can no longer read or change my data

requirements.text: Two devices are paired by scanning a QR code that carries a one-time token valid for `sync.pairing-ttl`.
Joining another device replaces the joining device's synced data with that device's; a device holding data of its own says what it holds and asks first, and a backup is taken before it is replaced.
A local change is synced within a few seconds while a paired device is reachable, and a Sync now button syncs on demand.
On Android the app also syncs in the background about every `sync.background-every`, on unmetered networks only.
Coming back to the front asks for a sync and reloads what is on screen; a drill or conversation in progress keeps its own data.
A device can be removed from the learner's devices; its key is revoked and it is refused from then on.
When two devices changed the same row without seeing each other, the later change wins, with ties settled by device id.
Append-only tables (the learning log, the mastery ledger, an answer's words) are written once by one device and never conflict.
A day's totals are kept per device and summed when read.
Settings about the device stay on it: theme, time zone, reminders, audio prefetch, repeat mode, haptics, speaking cards and the marks that say built-in content was seeded.
Work in progress is carried on only by the device that started it: a song being made, a picture being drawn, a tutor reply being written.
A database put back from an older copy is noticed and takes a new device identity before it syncs.
Devices sync only when their schema versions are equal, and debug and release builds never sync with each other.
Connections are encrypted with Noise, and a peer that is not one of the learner's devices, or whose key is revoked, is refused.
An interrupted sync resumes: changes are pulled in batches of at most `sync.batch-rows` rows and about 4 MB, applied in small transactions, and the bookmark moves only with a batch's last part.
On a computer that syncs with another device a snapshot of the database is kept daily: one a day for `snapshot.daily`, then one a week up to `snapshot.weekly-until`.
Android's own backup of the app's data is off.
Every synced table's triggers list all of its columns; a test fails otherwise.
